evidence: numerical-uncalibrated simulation and an illustrative animation; nothing built, flown or tested. All aero/propulsion/snow values ASSUMED unless marked CALC/LIT.
oneLine: v2 'throw-and-loiter': a 124 g folding flying wing with one pusher and a 16 g 4K camera on a micro-servo cradle; thrown at the top and airborne behind you before you push off (ready cue), loiters at stops (never lands), belly-lands beside you at the lift; worn bank recharges it on the lift. Works in calm–3 m/s for 9–13 m/s riders; fails the harmonised ensemble.
whyRedesign: v1 rebuilt on the shared component/battery table weighs 235 g → KE-cap speed 11.3 m/s, below a 13 m/s rider; hover + perch + relaunch were the mass and the catch-up loss.
Every launch/landing at stops is the cost: v2 never lands mid-run; the only launch happens before the push-off, so the rider's own acceleration is the catch-up window.

No brushless gimbal (30 g): body-fixed camera was tested and rejected (avail 25.6 % light wind: banked turns push the rider out of a 120° lens and the wide lens costs native pixels); a 3-servo cradle (12.5 g) + gyro stabilisation keeps an 80° lens (native 1080p crop).

ideasEvaluated.idea: never land at stops: loiter/orbit or slope-soar
ideasEvaluated.result: adopted; orbit ≈10.5 W electrical in calm (2.1 W drag power), into-wind station keeping ≥3.5 m/s; terrain-following slope flow modelled (w_z = −tanθ·w_x)

ideasEvaluated.idea: perch on the skier (pack-top) with a wake shield
ideasEvaluated.result: rejected: needs hover authority (v1 dock sims: props 0.18 m from the helmet at 3 m/s, 0.93 m miss at 9 m/s) and the hover motors that make it too heavy for the KE cap

ideasEvaluated.idea: take off before the skier pushes off / push-off signal
ideasEvaluated.result: adopted: hand throw at the top, tag vibrates 'ready' when it is ≥4 m up, behind and heading down the fall line; catch-up to <10 m in 1.2 s (calm). Costs ≈8 s standstill at the top.

ideasEvaluated.idea: lighter imaging chain (no gimbal, EIS crop)
ideasEvaluated.result: rejected after test: fixed 120° camera light-wind avail 25.6 % vs 75.4 % with the servo cradle
not adopted: adds the reel/line and the stop dock of the towglider without its in-motion launch; dominated by towglider itself

ideasEvaluated.idea: gravity potential: bank height while waiting, dive to catch up
ideasEvaluated.result: adopted implicitly (zoom-climb at the stop, loiter 7 m up); it does not beat the KE cap — only lag at the moment the rider reaches full speed matters (closing speed ≈1–1.7 m/s)
adopted (fail-safe landing off the track); plus a 5.5 m/s wind interlock because loiter airspeed + wind exceeds the KE-cap ground speed

chosenArchitecture.airframe: flying wing 0.065 m², 0.66 m span, scissor fold to 35×12.5×6 cm, CD0 0.050, CLmax 0.8, stall 6.8 m/s
chosenArchitecture.propulsion: one 1104-class motor, 3.5″ folding pusher, 1.1 N static; wind-milling regen ≤1C
chosenArchitecture.camera: 16 g 4K module with gyro log, 80° lens, 3-axis micro-servo cradle (τ 0.08 s), ≥40° subject-locked crop, 10 % gyro-stabilisation residual
chosenArchitecture.energy: 2.0 Wh flying cell (13.3 g at 150 Wh/kg) + 18.5 Wh worn bank; heated sleeve charges on the lift

userSequence: top: draw from the heated sleeve (wing springs open), throw from the shoulder across the slope / into the wind (action 1)
wait for the tag vibration (≈8 s), push off — it is already airborne behind you
ski: gravity-paid follow 4.5 m behind / 2.6 m up, pusher mostly folded
mid-run stop: it zoom-climbs and orbits/station-keeps up-slope 7 m up; no landing
lift approach: it flies a short pattern and belly-lands ≈3.5–6 m beside you; step over, pick it up, slide it into the sleeve (action 2); bank recharges it on the lift
envelope: calm–3 m/s wind (no 6 m/s+ flight: interlock), groomed 15° piste, steady riders 9–13 m/s (avail 80–91 %), stops ≥10 s apart; 3 m/s up-slope/down-slope wind already costs 2/3 landing crashes or 50–66 % avail; >14 m/s riders are outrun (avail 6–8 % at 15 m/s); short turns 70 %, moguls 65 %.
dominance: Dominated by towglider on the harmonised ensemble (setup, avail across wind). Niche where it is better: no line at all (no snag/bystander line hazard, no body force), free aerial viewpoint incl. an overhead view of the stopped rider, calm bluebird days on open pistes for steady recreational carvers.
honestLimits: Standstill 33–35 s even in calm (fails ≤30 s): top ready cue ≈8 s after the throw + end landing wait ≈12 s.
Mid-run restart not synchronised with the loiter: ≈11 s to be within 10 m again at 3 m/s.
Landing in up-slope 3 m/s wind crashed in 2/3 seeds; 6–9 m/s → no follow (interlock); one 6 m/s tailwind run slipped past the interlock to 18 J and 70 m range.
Attitude disturbance is one-way (camera only); throw, belly-skid friction and touchdown tolerance ASSUMED; regulation outside the model (US VLOS, resort bans).
